steps.body: Beyond direction, look at three things. **Clusters**: groups of dots bunched together. **Outliers**: lone dots far from the rest. **Form**: whether the pattern follows a straight line (**linear**) or a curve (**nonlinear**).
Fit the main rising band while one point remains visibly far from it.

widget.prompt: Fit the overall trend of the seven points. Notice what the one high point does to the residual gaps.
widget.successFeedback: The fitted line still rises with the main band. The lone high point is an outlier: important to investigate, but not enough to erase the overall pattern.
widget.slopeFeedback: Follow the six-point rising band first. One unusual point should not make the fitted line ignore the rest of the data.
widget.offsetFeedback: The direction is plausible, but the line is not centered on the main band. Adjust its vertical position.

predict.prompt: One point sits far from a rising band. Does that point erase the overall pattern?

options.label: No; the band remains and the point is unusual
Yes; one outlier removes the whole pattern
The point must be a recording mistake

predict.reveal: A point far from the main band is an outlier. It deserves attention, but the direction of the larger group still provides evidence of an association.

steps.body: Form tells you what kind of model fits. If the dots follow a straight path, the form is linear and a straight line summarizes them. If they bend — leveling off or curving up — the form is nonlinear and a line would miss the shape.

explanationVariants: Dots following a straight rising path have a linear form.
A straight-line pattern is linear form.

widget.prompt: The dots on a scatter plot follow a straight, steadily rising path. What is the form?

options.label: Linear
options.feedback: Right — a straight-path pattern has linear form.

options.label: Nonlinear
options.feedback: Nonlinear patterns CURVE — a straight path is linear.

options.label: No form
options.feedback: A steady straight path is a clear linear form.

options.label: Cluster
options.feedback: A cluster is about grouping, not form — a straight path is linear form.

widget.prompt: The dots rise steeply at first, then level off into a flat curve. What is the form?

options.label: Nonlinear
options.feedback: Right — a bending, leveling pattern is nonlinear.

options.label: Linear
options.feedback: Linear means a STRAIGHT path — this one curves and levels off, so it's nonlinear.

options.label: Positive only
options.feedback: That describes direction, not form — the curving shape makes the FORM nonlinear.

options.label: No association
options.feedback: There IS a pattern (it rises then levels) — the form is nonlinear.

explanationVariants: A cluster is a group of dots bunched in one region, showing many items with similar values.
Clusters mark where many data points share similar values.

widget.prompt: On a scatter plot, several dots are tightly bunched in the lower-left corner. What does this cluster tell you?

options.label: Many items have low values on both measures
options.feedback: Right — a cluster marks a group with similar values.

options.label: One item lies far from the other points
options.feedback: An outlier is a LONE far-off dot — a bunched GROUP is a cluster.

options.label: The relationship has a negative direction
options.feedback: A cluster's location doesn't set direction — it shows a group of similar values.

options.label: The relationship follows a curved form
options.feedback: Bunching is a cluster, not form — form is about straight vs. curved.

explanationVariants: An outlier can pull a summary line away from the main pattern, so it is worth noticing.
Outliers can distort a fitted line, so flag them.

widget.prompt: Why is it important to notice an outlier before drawing a summary line?

options.label: It can pull the line away from the main pattern
options.feedback: Right — a far-off point can drag a fitted line off the true trend.

options.label: It is always a mistake to delete
options.feedback: Outliers aren't automatically errors — the point is they can DISTORT a line, so notice them.

options.label: It changes the axis labels
options.feedback: An outlier doesn't relabel axes — it can pull a summary line off the pattern.

options.label: It has no effect
options.feedback: It CAN affect the line — a far-off point drags the summary away from the trend.

explanationVariants: Bunched group = cluster; lone far dot = outlier; straight path = linear; curved path = nonlinear.
Match each description to cluster, outlier, or form.

widget.prompt: Sort each scatter-plot feature by what it describes.

items.label: a group of dots bunched together
items.feedback: A bunched group is a cluster.

items.label: one lone dot far from the rest
items.feedback: A single far-off dot is an outlier.

items.label: the dots follow a straight line
items.feedback: Straight vs. curved describes the form (here, linear).

items.label: the dots bend into a curve
items.feedback: A curved pattern describes the form (here, nonlinear).

items.label: a single point sitting way above the trend
items.feedback: A lone point off the trend is an outlier.

widget.missFeedback: Not quite — a bunched group is a cluster, a lone far dot is an outlier, and straight-vs-curved is form.
widget.successFeedback: All sorted — clusters group, outliers stand alone, and form is the straight-or-curved shape.

hints: A cluster is a GROUP; an outlier is a LONE dot far away.
Form is about the shape of the pattern: straight or curved.
Clusters: bunched group. Outliers: lone far dot / point above the trend. Form: straight (linear) or curved (nonlinear).

steps.body: Describe a scatter plot by its clusters, outliers, and form — not just its direction.
takeaways: Clusters are groups of similar values; outliers are lone far-off dots.
Outliers can pull a summary line off the main pattern.
steps.teaser: Next chapter: fitting a straight line to the data.

concept.body: Describe a scatter plot by its clusters (bunched groups), outliers (lone far-off dots), and form: linear (straight path) or nonlinear (curved path).

explanationVariants: A pattern that curves and levels off is nonlinear.
A bending, curving path has nonlinear form.

widget.prompt: The dots on a scatter plot rise then bend into a curve. What is the form?

options.label: Nonlinear
options.feedback: Right — a curved, bending path is nonlinear form.

options.label: Linear
options.feedback: Linear is a STRAIGHT path — this curves, so it's nonlinear.

options.label: Cluster
options.feedback: Clusters are about grouping — a curved path describes form (nonlinear).

options.label: Outlier
options.feedback: An outlier is a lone dot — a curved PATTERN is nonlinear form.
